messages:
Samir: Heads-up — after the cost-smoothing changes landed, we've seen a ~7% spike in route churn for tiered customers. Dumping telemetry now.
Elaine: ack, saw that on the dashboard. mostly 99th-tail reads bouncing between dedicated and hosted variants
Todd: any obvious correlation with sequence length or region?
Samir: looks like eu-west requests are the worst, and sequences >1k. Cost cap kicks in, policy recomputes, then routing picks a cheaper variant that can't keep up -> retry, back to expensive. oscillation.
Jen: so it's a feedback loop between cost-driven policy and capacity signals.
Samir: exactly. Proposed fix: decouple short-term stability heuristics from policy-eval. Keep policy stateless; implement a thin "route-stability cache" in the runtime that biases recent successful route choices for X secs.
Elaine: yeah prefer runtime-side sticky routing rather than baking timers into the policy DSL.
Todd: agree. Stateful timers in the policy engine will make hot-reload and sandboxing harder.
Jen: can we expose the window as a policy opt so tenants can tune? e.g. stability_window_ms
Samir: we can, but don't let the policy code manage state. Policy returns a scored list; runtime applies smoothing using: final_score = alpha*cached_score + (1-alpha)*policy_score.
Samir: example config snippet:
```
policy: {
  name: "tiered-cost-latency",
  stability_hint_ms: 120000,
  cost_weight: 0.6,
  latency_weight: 0.4
}
```
Elaine: and then runtime has per-route cache with TTL=stability_hint_ms and decay alpha function.
ops-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-477 route-churn-eu-west (linked)
Todd: important: telemetry gap. current route telemetry is aggregated per-minute, so we miss sub-minute oscillation. Need higher-granularity counters for canary window.
Samir: agreed. short term: increase route-event granularity to 10s for a 24h window for affected services.
Jen: long term: instrument per-request route decision traces and sample 1% to S3 for offline sims.
Elaine: can we implement a lightweight priority queue for fallbacks? if cached route fails N times within M secs, runtime should suppress it for a cooldown.
Samir: yes — cooldown + exponential backoff is good. keep parameters runtime-only.
Todd: impacts for dedup/cache? need to ensure prefix/KV hits don't get stale when we suppress route.
Samir: open question. propose an invariant: only suppress a route if failure is at transport/serve layer, not logical result mismatch.
Jen: perf concerns: smoothing adds another step to hot path. we should microbenchmark overhead <3% p99.
Elaine: I'll own a small experiment: implement runtime sticky layer + cooldown + 10s telemetry. Canary on eu-west, 10% traffic, 24h.
Samir: thanks. follow-ups: (1) infra to bump telemetry retention/granularity (Todd) (2) runtime PR for sticky cache + cooldown (Elaine) (3) sims from sampled traces to validate heuristics (Jen) (4) update policy docs to recommend runtime tuning knobs (Samir)
Todd: ping @infra-bot for quota
infra-bot: noted. spinning up short-lived high-card telemetry stream for 24h on eu-west, quota assigned.
Samir: one more thing — keep policy DSL minimal: no timers, no cooldown primitives. We can add hints (stability_hint_ms) and allow runtime to interpret.
Elaine: +1. keeps sandbox/testability clean.
Jen: will add a short RFC blurb recommending the decoupled approach and include the config snippet + experiment plan.
Samir: cool. thanks all. I'll monitor the canary and post numbers in ~12h. :thumbsup:
